lean.statement:
have π :=
  (3 / 8) • Measure.dirac (false, false) + (1 / 8) • Measure.dirac (false, true) +
      (1 / 8) • Measure.dirac (true, false) +
    (3 / 8) • Measure.dirac (true, true);
have P := Kernel.ofFunOfCountable fun x => (3 / 4) • Measure.dirac (x.2, x.2) + (1 / 4) • Measure.dirac (!x.2, x.2);
have Q := Kernel.ofFunOfCountable fun x => (3 / 4) • Measure.dirac (x.1, x.1) + (1 / 4) • Measure.dirac (x.1, !x.1);
IsProbabilityMeasure π ∧
  (∀ (x : Bool × Bool), 0 < π {x}) ∧
    IsMarkovKernel P ∧
      IsMarkovKernel Q ∧
        (∀ (b : Bool), π {z | z.2 = b} = 1 / 2 ∧ π {z | z.1 = b} = 1 / 2) ∧
          (∀ (x y : Bool × Bool), (P x) {y} = if y.2 = x.2 then 2 * π {y} else 0) ∧
            (∀ (x y : Bool × Bool), (Q x) {y} = if y.1 = x.1 then 2 * π {y} else 0) ∧
              P.IsReversible π ∧ Q.IsReversible π ∧ (Q ∘ₖ P).Invariant π ∧ ¬(Q ∘ₖ P).IsReversible π
approved_definition_context: The type Bool × Bool has exactly four discrete states. Measure.dirac is a point mass, and the displayed weights and singleton evaluations are extended nonnegative reals.

Kernel.ofFunOfCountable turns the displayed row measure into an actual kernel on a countable measurable-singleton space. IsMarkovKernel means every row is a probability. Kernel.IsReversible is equality of both stationary set fluxes; Kernel.Invariant says the target pushed along the kernel is unchanged.
Q ∘ₖ P applies P first, then Q. Printed have binders are local definitions, not premises; ! denotes Boolean negation.
